data.title: Dundee's (TSE:DC.A) Earnings Are Built On Soft Foundations
data.description:
Investors appear disappointed with Dundee Corporation's (TSE:DC.A) recent earnings, despite the decent statutory profit number. We did some digging and found some worrying factors that they might be paying attention to.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Zooming In On Dundee's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Dundee recorded an accrual ratio of 0.48. Ergo, its free cash flow is significantly weaker than its profit. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of CA$4.8m, which is significantly less than its profit of CA$203.1m. Given that Dundee had negative free cash flow in the prior corresponding period, the trailing twelve month resul of CA$4.8m would seem to be a step in the right direction. However, that's not all there is to consider. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part.

Check out our latest analysis for Dundee

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Dundee.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that Dundee's profit was boosted by unusual items worth CA$209m in the last twelve months. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. When we analysed the vast majority of listed companies worldwide, we found that significant unusual items are often not repeated. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Dundee had a rather significant contribution from unusual items relative to its profit to September 2026. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit a poor guide to underlying earnings power.

Our Take On Dundee's Profit Performance

Dundee had a weak accrual ratio, but its profit did receive a boost from unusual items. For all the reasons mentioned above, we think that, at a glance, Dundee's statutory profits could be considered to be low quality, because they are likely to give investors an overly positive impression of the company. So if you'd like to dive deeper into this stock, it's crucial to consider any risks it's facing. Our analysis shows 3 warning signs for Dundee (1 shouldn't be ignored!) and we strongly recommend you look at them before investing.

In this article we've looked at a number of factors that can impair the utility of profit numbers, and we've come away cautious. data.title: 3 ETFs That Give You Baidu After The Nvidia Chip Scrutiny
data.description:
You might like Baidu and its mix of search, video and AI work, but holding the stock on its own means you carry its specific issues yourself. Simply Wall St flags large one off items that can shake reported results, along with ongoing pressure in advertising where delays in making money from AI search could weigh on revenue and margins. Owning Baidu through a fund that also holds other companies changes how much these swings can move your overall portfolio, and it also limits how much any single winner can lift it.

The latest twist is about chips, not clicks. On 19 November 2026 the Commerce Department approved sales of advanced Nvidia processors, including 43,000 H200 chips, to Baidu and other Chinese firms while lawmakers questioned the oversight of such deals. That decision affects how much computing power Baidu can access for AI projects. It also frames how you might prefer to hold it, whether through CQQQ, SOCL or PGJ inside a broader basket.

Would you rather build your own basket around Baidu? Explore 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Invesco China Technology ETF (CQQQ)

PDD Holdings and Meituan anchor CQQQ at the top, so a lot of your money rides on Chinese e commerce and local services alongside Baidu. Tencent adds a large social and gaming tilt. Baidu is the fourth biggest position at 6.62% of the fund, which means each US$1,000 in CQQQ quietly tucks about US$66 into Baidu while the rest spreads across 222 holdings in areas such as restaurants, semiconductors and software.

Large one off items can move Baidu’s reported results in ways that do not match its underlying operations. CQQQ cannot blunt swings that hit the wider Chinese tech sector, but holdings tied to different revenue sources, such as food delivery, retail platforms and hardware, provide a broader mix than Baidu stock alone.

Compare how far CQQQ is ahead of or behind the market across six periods

Global X Social Media ETF (SOCL)

SOCL gives you Baidu as the #7 holding at 4.96% of the portfolio, so only a small slice of your money tracks Baidu directly. Each US$1,000 in SOCL puts roughly US$50 into Baidu. Most of your outcome instead comes from other social platforms. Tencent and Meta Platforms together are 19.6% of the fund, and NAVER also has a sizeable position. The industry split tilts heavily to Interactive Media and Services, with smaller pieces in Movies and Entertainment and Interactive Home Entertainment. This provides a broad social and online entertainment mix around Baidu.

Baidu has flagged that advertising is under strain while AI search monetization lags, so weak ad trends could affect its revenue and margins for longer than some market participants expect. SOCL still concentrates heavily in digital advertising and social media through Tencent, Meta Platforms and other Interactive Media and Services holdings, so a broad slowdown in online marketing would influence much of this portfolio as well. That mix provides company level diversification away from Baidu’s single stock moves but still leaves you exposed if social and ad driven business models face pressure at the same time.

Invesco Golden Dragon China ETF (PGJ)

PGJ leans heavily into Chinese consumer and internet industries, with Broadline Retail, restaurants and travel-related groups making up a large slice of its holdings. Yum China Holdings and JD.com together account for 18.4% of the ETF, so your money tracks both food services and online retail alongside Baidu. Baidu ranks as the #5 position at 5.59% of the portfolio, so each US$1,000 in PGJ holds about US$56 of Baidu within a mix that also includes education, entertainment, autos and transport.

Large one-off items can move Baidu’s reported financial results away from what its day-to-day operations suggest. PGJ’s exposure to sectors such as Broadline Retail and Restaurants can soften the impact of company-specific surprises tied to Baidu’s own projects or accounting items, yet you still end up relying heavily on how Chinese consumer and service-oriented businesses perform as a group.

Ten companies make up 59.3% of PGJ. Find out which ones, and how much each carries.

Choose how you want Baidu to sit

You are really choosing what you want wrapped around Baidu. CQQQ gives the biggest slice of Baidu at about US$66 per US$1,000, inside a China tech mix that leans on internet platforms, retail and hardware. PGJ holds a little less Baidu per US$1,000 but spreads your money across 69 holdings, with a larger tilt to Chinese consumer and travel industries. SOCL puts around US$50 of each US$1,000 into Baidu and clusters the rest in global social and entertainment platforms, so it is closest to a social media sector fund.

All three charge roughly US$65 to US$70 a year on US$10,000, and the recent chip approval news shows how policy shifts can ripple through Baidu’s AI plans. Large one off items can still distort Baidu’s reported numbers. The real fork for you is simple: do you care more about holding Baidu alongside broader China consumer trends, global social platforms, or a wider China tech basket, given that the Baidu weight only moves a few dozen dollars either way per US$1,000?

data.title: What Adobe Doubters Saw Before The Drop
data.description:
Adobe has had a packed year, from record quarterly revenue to a sweeping leadership handover and a huge new buyback plan, all while AI-first tools like Firefly reworked how creatives use its software. Holding Adobe from the start of the year would have meant a 33.5% loss, including dividends. If you had made that call on 1 January, how much of today’s debate about freemium AI, margins and user growth would you be expecting management to answer next?

The Two Adobe Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$350 at the start of the period, and you were choosing between two very different stories about what Adobe’s AI push might deliver.

On the upbeat side, the Firefly and GenStudio narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$456, a theoretical price implied by assumptions such as revenue growth of 8.8% and a 29.2% profit margin supported by deeper enterprise integration.

The more cautious view saw Firefly and AI assistants still drawing new users but assigned a Fair Value of US$280, with concerns that execution risks and pressure on revenue and margins could weigh on the business.

What The Adobe Evidence Actually Tested

Adobe’s record Q3 2026 revenue of US$6.76b and higher net income supported the upbeat case that Firefly, GenStudio and AI-first products could lift the top line. The drop in net margin from 29.6% to 27.0%, together with concerns about freemium AI pressure on revenue and profitability, kept the cautious view alive. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The episode turned on one assumption: higher AI usage had to show up not just in revenue, but in stable or improving profitability. For any other software stock, track the combination of ARR growth, reported net margin and how management explains freemium or AI giveaways in earnings calls.

What Adobe’s Share Price Drop Is Asking You To Believe

Adobe trades at US$222 from the start of the year, with the share price down 33.5%. This Narrative’s Fair Value sits above the current price, which according to BlackJesus, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative, reflects a market that has leaned heavily into AI fear.

The argument hinges on Adobe’s role in professional, brand-safe workflows rather than casual content. For the Narrative’s higher figure to be reached, buyers today would need to assume Firefly and related tools convert enterprise AI usage into durable, paid subscription and credit demand.

data.title: There's A Lot To Like About Build-A-Bear Workshop's (NYSE:BBW) Upcoming US$0.23 Dividend
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Build-A-Bear Workshop, Inc. (NYSE:BBW) is about to go ex-dividend in just four days. The ex-dividend date is one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. Therefore, if you purchase Build-A-Bear Workshop's shares on or after the 25th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 7th of January.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.23 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of US$0.92 per share. Based on the last year's worth of payments, Build-A-Bear Workshop has a trailing yield of 3.2% on the current stock price of US$28.87. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether Build-A-Bear Workshop's dividend is reliable and sustainable. We need to see whether the dividend is covered by earnings and if it's growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid from company earnings. If a company pays more in dividends than it earned in profit, then the dividend could be unsustainable. Build-A-Bear Workshop is paying out just 22% of its profit after tax, which is comfortably low and leaves plenty of breathing room in the case of adverse events. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. Fortunately, it paid out only 47% of its free cash flow in the past year.

It's encouraging to see that the dividend is covered by both profit and cash flow. This generally suggests the dividend is sustainable, as long as earnings don't drop precipitously.

See our latest analysis for Build-A-Bear Workshop

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with consistently growing earnings per share generally make the best dividend stocks, as they usually find it easier to grow dividends per share. If earnings fall far enough, the company could be forced to cut its dividend. For this reason, we're glad to see Build-A-Bear Workshop's earnings per share have risen 10% per annum over the last five years. Earnings per share are growing rapidly and the company is keeping more than half of its earnings within the business; an attractive combination which could suggest the company is focused on reinvesting to grow earnings further. Fast-growing businesses that are reinvesting heavily are enticing from a dividend perspective, especially since they can often increase the payout ratio later.

Many investors will assess a company's dividend performance by evaluating how much the dividend payments have changed over time. Build-A-Bear Workshop has delivered an average of 4.8% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past three years of dividend payments. Earnings per share have been growing much quicker than dividends, potentially because Build-A-Bear Workshop is keeping back more of its profits to grow the business.

Final Takeaway

Has Build-A-Bear Workshop got what it takes to maintain its dividend payments? We love that Build-A-Bear Workshop is growing earnings per share while simultaneously paying out a low percentage of both its earnings and cash flow. These characteristics suggest the company is reinvesting in growing its business, while the conservative payout ratio also implies a reduced risk of the dividend being cut in the future. Overall we think this is an attractive combination and worthy of further research.

While it's tempting to invest in Build-A-Bear Workshop for the dividends alone, you should always be mindful of the risks involved. To that end, you should learn about the 3 warning signs we've spotted with Build-A-Bear Workshop (including 2 which are a bit concerning).

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On eGain's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, eGain recorded an accrual ratio of -0.37. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. To wit, it produced free cash flow of US$12m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of US$7.61m. eGain did see its free cash flow drop year on year, which is less than ideal, like a Simpson's episode without Groundskeeper Willie.

Our Take On eGain's Profit Performance

Based on this observation, we consider it possible that eGain's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! Better yet, its EPS are growing strongly, which is nice to see. A Closer Look At Intellicheck's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Intellicheck has an accrual ratio of -0.21 for the year to September 2026. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. In fact, it had free cash flow of US$5.6m in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of US$3.32m. Intellicheck's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

data.title: Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV:OMAB) Is About To Go Ex-Dividend, And It Pays A 4.7% Yield
data.description:
Readers hoping to buy Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV:OMAB) for its dividend will need to make their move shortly, as the stock is about to trade ex-dividend. The ex-dividend date is commonly two business days before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. It is important to be aware of the ex-dividend date because any trade on the stock needs to have been settled on or before the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de's shares before the 24th of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 25th of November.

The company's upcoming dividend is Mex$6.280254 a share, following on from the last 12 months, when the company distributed a total of Mex$11.54 per share to shareholders. Looking at the last 12 months of distributions, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de has a trailing yield of approximately 4.7% on its current stock price of Mex$246.32. Dividends are an important source of income to many shareholders, but the health of the business is crucial to maintaining those dividends. We need to see whether the dividend is covered by earnings and if it's growing.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

If a company pays out more in dividends than it earned, then the dividend might become unsustainable - hardly an ideal situation. Its dividend payout ratio is 84% of profit, which means the company is paying out a majority of its earnings. The relatively limited profit reinvestment could slow the rate of future earnings growth. We'd be worried about the risk of a drop in earnings. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. Over the past year it paid out 121% of its free cash flow as dividends, which is uncomfortably high. It's hard to consistently pay out more cash than you generate without either borrowing or using company cash, so we'd wonder how the company justifies this payout level.

While Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de's dividends were covered by the company's reported profits, cash is somewhat more important, so it's not great to see that the company didn't generate enough cash to pay its dividend. Cash is king, as they say, and were Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de to repeatedly pay dividends that aren't well covered by cashflow, we would consider this a warning sign.

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Stocks in companies that generate sustainable earnings growth often make the best dividend prospects, as it is easier to lift the dividend when earnings are rising. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. It's encouraging to see Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de has grown its earnings rapidly, up 38% a year for the past five years. Earnings have been growing quickly, but we're concerned dividend payments consumed most of the company's cash flow over the past year.

Many investors will assess a company's dividend performance by evaluating how much the dividend payments have changed over time. In the last 10 years, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de has lifted its dividend by approximately 13% a year on average. Both per-share earnings and dividends have both been growing rapidly in recent times, which is great to see.

Final Takeaway

Is Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de worth buying for its dividend? It's good to see that earnings per share are growing and that the company's payout ratio is within a normal range for most businesses. However we're somewhat concerned that it paid out 121% of its cashflow, which is uncomfortably high. In summary, it's hard to get excited about Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte. de from a dividend perspective.
